transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. 

Um, well, I guess what brought me in is... my supervisor at the plant told me I should probably talk to someone. It's really not a huge deal, I promise, I just... well, I have this little habit of leaving my work station? Or like, during our shift meetings when everybody is supposed to stay put, I just sort of pop up out of my chair. 

I really don't mean to be disruptive or anything, I swear! I just kind of take off before I even think about it. But my supervisor says it's actually becoming a safety problem on the floor, so I wanted to come in and do whatever I need to do to fix it, so I don't cause any trouble for them. Is... is that the kind of thing you can help with? Am I explaining that okay?
Do you often feel restless or have trouble staying seated even when you're not at work or in meetings?

Um, well... I guess I do get a little antsy sometimes? I hope that doesn't sound too bad. 

It's just... like, when I try to stand still by my machine on the line, or if I have to sit through one of our training sessions, it almost feels like there's this, um, pressure building up inside my body? And I just feel like I absolutely have to move, or pace around a little, or stretch, or just go do something right then and there. 

I really try my best to fight it and be good, I promise! But it just gets so uncomfortable to stay still when that pressure starts. Does that make sense? Is that what you mean by restless?
Do you also feel this way when you're not at work, like when you're at home trying to relax or sit through a movie or a meal?

Oh, um... yeah, I guess so. I really hope I'm not sounding like a difficult person or anything! 

But um, yeah, even when I'm off the clock, quiet stuff just makes me feel a little... trapped? Like, even if I'm just trying to sit in the break room and read a manual, or if I'm at home trying to sit through a movie or something, I just can't seem to just be quiet. I always end up humming to myself, or tapping my feet, or I'll just start talking to whoever is around, or I just end up getting up entirely instead of relaxing. 

I really don't mean to ruin the movie or bother people in the break room, I swear! I just... I don't know, my body just won't let me do the quiet thing very well. Is that... is that the kind of answer you were looking for?
When did you first start feeling this way? Was it something you noticed even when you were a kid, or is it more recent?

Um... well, it's definitely not a new thing. I really hope it doesn't make me sound like I was a bad kid or anything! I always wanted to be good. 

But, um, yeah... even way back in elementary school, I guess I was kind of known as the girl who just couldn't stay in her seat. I didn't mean to be disrespectful to the teachers, I swear! But I would just sort of... blurt things out before they were done talking, or I'd end up wandering around the classroom when we were supposed to be doing quiet work. 

I got quite a few notes sent home about it, which always made me feel awful because I didn't want to cause trouble. It's just always been really hard for me to hold things in or stay put. I hope that's okay to admit? Does that help explain things?
Can you tell me if you’ve had similar difficulties staying still or controlling impulses in other settings besides work and school, like in social situations or when you're trying to relax at home?

Um, well... I guess I already mentioned home a little bit with the movies and stuff, but... I don't know if I have too many other examples? I really hope that's alright! I don't go out to a ton of social things, mostly just hang out with a couple friends sometimes. 

And when I'm with them, I try really hard to be a good listener and not interrupt, I really do! But... I guess maybe sometimes I still talk a little fast or get too excited and talk over them by accident? But they know I don't mean anything bad by it! 

I don't really know if I have a lot of other places where it happens, honestly. I try my best to keep it together when I'm out in public. I hope I'm giving you enough information... is it okay if I don't have a lot of other examples?
